title: Bias
body:
**"Bias" means two unrelated things in this folder and they are not variations on one idea.** Same
treatment as [[Complexity]], [[FIFO]], and [[Simulation]]: both senses, labelled, in the order the
vault's links mean them.

## Sense 1: the bias term (what [[Bias Term]] means)

The constant $b$ in $\mathbf{w} \cdot \mathbf{x} + b$, one per [[Neuron]]. It is a learned
parameter like any [[Weights|weight]], and it exists so the decision boundary does not have to pass
through the origin. It is the intercept of a line. **This is the sense every link in this folder
means**, and [[Bias Term]] owns it.

## Sense 2: statistical bias, and the bias-variance trade-off

An estimator is **biased** if its expected value is not the quantity it estimates:
$\mathbf{E}[\hat\theta] \neq \theta$. Nothing to do with the number $b$. See
[[Sampling Distribution]] in [[STATISTICS]] (MATH 2234), which owns the definition.

Applied to a fitted model, the expected error at a point decomposes into three pieces:

$$
\text{error} = \underbrace{\text{bias}^2}_{\text{wrong on average}} + \underbrace{\text{variance}}_{\text{unstable across samples}} + \underbrace{\text{noise}}_{\text{irreducible}}
$$

| | High bias | High variance |
|---|---|---|
| Cause | model too simple to represent the truth | model flexible enough to fit the sample's noise |
| Symptom | bad on training data *and* test data | good on training data, bad on test data |
| Usual name | underfitting | overfitting |
| Fix | bigger model, more features | more data, simpler model, regularisation |

**The trade-off is the point**: for a fixed amount of data, reducing one usually raises the other,
and only more data improves both. That is structurally the same statement as $\alpha$ against
$\beta$ in [[Type I and Type II Errors]], where more data is likewise the only escape from the
curve.

## Sense 3, worth naming: bias in the ethical sense

A model that reproduces the skew in its training data. Real, and not what either formula above is
about. The vault has no note on it.

## Related

- [[Bias Term]]: sense 1, the real note
- [[Sampling Distribution]] and [[Variance]] ([[STATISTICS]], MATH 2234): sense 2's machinery
- [[Stratification]]: the sampling fix that keeps a split from adding bias of its own
- [[Neuron]], [[Weights]]: where sense 1 lives
